speaker: Doctor
text: I have heard of your symptoms; to narrow this down, have you noticed any trouble swallowing or breathing difficulties as well? Additionally, has your condition been progressive or did it come on suddenly?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of weakness worsening with activity and improving with rest is very suggestive of a neuromuscular junction disorder. Have you noticed any drooping of your eyelids (ptosis) or difficulty speaking clearly? Additionally, do you experience muscle pain or cramping?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. I am requesting a Acetylcholine Receptor Antibody test and a Chest CT to rule out thymoma.
